title: Smooth base change for limits of smooth schemes
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and let $I$ be a nonempty directed set. Let $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system of schemes over $S$, with structure maps $g_i:S_i\to S$ which are smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Suppose $S'=\varprojlim_i S_i$, with induced structure map $g:S'\to S$. Let $f:X\to S$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and form the cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'=X\times_S S'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
S'&\xrightarrow{g}&S.
\end{array}
$$
Let $E\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ be a bounded below complex of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Assume its cohomology has torsion orders invertible on $S$: explicitly, for every integer $q$, every geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$, and every element $v\in\mathcal H^q(E)_{\bar x}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], there is a positive integer $n$ such that $nv=0$ and $n\cdot1$ is a unit in $\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$. No common annihilator is required. Then the canonical bounded below derived exchange morphism [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]
$$
\Ex_{\square,E}:g^{-1}Rf_*E\longrightarrow Rf'_*g'^{-1}E
$$
is an isomorphism in $\Dplus(S'_{\Et})$. Here $u^{-1}$ and $Ru_*$ are inverse image and derived direct image of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. This is Stacks Tag 0F09 in the case in which the maps $S_i\to S$ are also quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

proof.text: Put $X_i=X\times_S S_i$, with projections $g'_i:X_i\to X$ and $f_i:X_i\to S_i$. These are cartesian squares in the convention of [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. For $j\ge i$, $X_j\to X_i$ is the base change of $S_j\to S_i$, so is affine by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. The constant systems $S$ and $X$ have affine identity transitions as well. The limit of $(X_i)$ is $X'$, without any assumption that $S$ is quasi-compact: a compatible cone $T\to X_i$ gives maps $T\to X$ all equal (use a common upper bound for any two indices) and a compatible family $T\to S_i$, hence a unique map $T\to S'$. Their composites to $S$ agree, so the fibre-product universal property gives a unique map $T\to X'$, inducing the original cone. Conversely a map to $X'$ gives this cone. This proves the required limit universal property.

First let $F$ be an abelian etale sheaf on $X$ with torsion orders invertible on $S$ as explicitly defined in the statement, and fix $p\ge0$. Apply [sbc-thm-smooth-base-change] with its four corners $(X,Y,S,T)=(S_i,X_i,S,X)$ and its morphisms $(f,g,h,e)=(g_i,f,f_i,g'_i)$. Its smooth leg is $g_i$, its quasi-compact and quasi-separated leg is the given $f$, and its coefficient sheaf is $F$ on $X$, with orders invertible on the same base $S$. All of these are hypotheses already in force. It gives the canonical sheaf base-change isomorphism
$$g_i^{-1}R^pf_*F\xrightarrow{\sim}R^pf_{i,*}(g'_i)^{-1}F$$
for every $i$. In particular we do not require the limit map $g$ itself to be smooth.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-kun-0ezt] to the transposed inverse system: its corners $(X_i,Y_i,S_i,T_i)$ are $(S_i,X_i,S,X)$, and its arrows $(f_i,h_i,e_i,g_i)$ are $(g_i,f_i,g'_i,f)$. In particular the direct-image leg called $g_i$ in that lemma is the constant map $f:X\to S$, which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Its coefficient system on the constant corner $T_i=X$ is $F_i=F$ with identity transition maps, not the sheaves $(g'_i)^{-1}F$ on $X_i$. This is a compatible system of torsion sheaves and its limit coefficient is $F$: a cocone from the constant identity diagram is exactly a single map from $F$, since $I$ is nonempty and directed. All four systems have affine transitions and the limits identified in Step 1. The finite-stage base-change maps required by that lemma are precisely the maps of Step 2. Its conclusion is therefore
$$g^{-1}R^pf_*F\xrightarrow{\sim}R^pf'_*g'^{-1}F.$$
This proves the sheaf assertion for every $p\ge0$.

proof.text:
Choose $a\in\mathbf Z$ with $\mathcal H^q(E)=0$ for $q<a$, and put $\Phi=g^{-1}Rf_*$ and $\Psi=Rf'_*g'^{-1}$ on bounded below derived categories of abelian sheaves. Use the two truncation couples, on $S'$, of [def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations], parts (2) and (3). Their first pages are
$$E_2^{p,q}=g^{-1}R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(E),\qquad E_2'^{p,q}=R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(E).$$
The first is already pulled back to $S'$; we do not compare sheaves on different bases. Clauses (1)--(3) of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-couple-morphism] give exact couples and a morphism of them induced by $\Ex_\square$, with first-page component $\mathcal H^p(\Ex_{\square,\mathcal H^q(E)})$. By [lem-kun-bc-map-on-cohomology] this component is exactly the usual sheaf base-change map in Step 3, hence is an isomorphism for $p\ge0$. For $p<0$ both higher direct images vanish, as that same node states, so it is an isomorphism there too. Each sheaf $\mathcal H^q(E)$ satisfies the coefficient condition by assumption. Now [lem-sp-couple-morphism] supplies a compatible morphism on all spectral-sequence pages.

proof.text: An isomorphism on page $r$ commuting with differentials induces an isomorphism on page $r+1$: it carries the kernels of the differentials bijectively to the corresponding kernels and their images bijectively to the corresponding images, hence induces an inverse on the quotients defining cohomology. Starting with Step 4 proves that the maps on every page are isomorphisms. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-convergence] to these couples: $E$ is bounded below by $a$ and has torsion cohomology, so for fixed total degree $n\ge a$ there are only $0\le p\le n-a$, $q=n-p$, and all these terms have stabilized by $r=n-a+2$. Thus their $E_\infty$ maps are isomorphisms. By clauses (2)--(4) of [lemma-weil-pbc-exact-couple-abutment], the resulting map on the actual abutments is $\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\square,E})$, it preserves their finite filtrations, and its maps on associated graded pieces are precisely those $E_\infty$ maps. Apply [lem-sp-finite-filtration-induction] to conclude that $\mathcal H^n(\Ex_{\square,E})$ is an isomorphism. For $n<a$ both abutments vanish: the finite-filtration assertion of the convergence node gives $F^0H^n=H^n$ and also $F^0H^n=0$ since $0\ge n-a+1$. Hence the same conclusion holds for every integer $n$.

proof.text: The exchange is a morphism in $\Dplus(S'_{\Et})$. Step 5 shows it is an isomorphism on every cohomology sheaf. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology], with the abelian category of abelian etale sheaves on $S'$, to conclude that $\Ex_{\square,E}$ is an isomorphism, as asserted.
